title: How Airlines Really Make Money: Credit Cards
description:
In 2025 American Airlines earned $111 million in net profit, while its co-branded credit card and other partners paid it $6.2 billion in cash. American Express paid Delta $8.2 billion, more than Delta's $6.2 billion pre-tax profit and about 13% of its revenue. The trick: airlines sell miles to banks, get cash today, and provide the seat later.

Sources: American Airlines Group 2025 Form 10-K and Q4 2025 earnings release (Jan 27, 2026); Delta Air Lines December quarter and full-year 2025 results (Jan 13, 2026). Partner payments are revenue, not profit.

scenes.say: In twenty twenty-five, American Airlines made a hundred and eleven million dollars in profit. Its credit card and other partners paid it six point two billion.
A big reason: airlines don't just sell seats. They sell miles. Banks buy them in bulk and give them to you as card rewards.
Delta's card partner, American Express, paid it eight point two billion dollars in twenty twenty-five.

visual.label: paid to Delta by American Express

scenes.say: That's more than Delta's entire pre-tax profit of six point two billion, and about one in every eight dollars it brought in.
Why do airlines love it? They get the cash today, and only provide the seat later, when you redeem.
So you might be the passenger. But one of the airline's biggest customers is your bank.
